newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs say Israelis ransack school, Korans torn.
newsitem.headline: Arabs say Israelis ransack school, Korans torn.

text.p: Palestinians said on Sunday they found torn copies of the Koran in a school they charged was ransacked by Israeli soldiers in the strife-torn West Bank town of Hebron.
An Israeli officer denied the charges after touring the school with his Palestinian counterpart.

Hebron was mainly quiet on Sunday but has been the scene of almost daily clashes since an Israeli woman put up posters on Palestinian shops depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig stamping on the Koran nine days ago.

Israeli television broadcast pictures of a room in Hebron's al-Yaacoubiya girls school in which furniture had been overturned, paint splattered on the walls and pictures of Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat torn.
Several copies of the Koran with some pages falling out or ripped were among a litter of papers and books scattered on the floor. Arabic grafitti on the walls bore the name of Arafat's Fatah faction.

"The army always breaks the door and comes in to use the roof to watch demonstrators. They broke furniture and we found four Koran books torn and thrown on the ground," said the elementary school's headmaster, Arifeh Ebedo.
"Where are the Moslems all over the world who see their holy books torn, thrown and trampled?" she said.
Reuters reporters saw Israeli soldiers inside the school and on its roof last Thursday after clashes nearby between troops and Palestinian protesters.
Israel's Hebron district liaison office chief Colonel Baruch Nagar toured the school with his Palestinian counterpart and school officials to investigate the incident.

"Colonel Nagar made clear and emphasised...that Israeli soldiers had no part in this incident," said Peter Lerner, spokesman for the Israeli military's Civil Administration in the occupied territories.

"The investigation showed that the room was locked and that soldiers did not have access to it...only a person with a key could enter the teachers' room and as proof of this there were no forced entry signs on the door," Lerner said.
The school is located on the seam between Israeli- and Palestinian-controlled areas of Hebron, the scene of almost daily Arab-Israeli violence in recent weeks.

"Today the situation is calming," Palestinian West Bank security chief Jibril Rajoub told Reuters. "Our people expressed themselves in a series of demonstrations last week. They did their national duty."
Israeli leaders have roundly condemned the posting of the pig posters.

A 26-year-old Jerusalem woman, Tatyana Suskin, was charged last week with illegally putting up the posters and endangering life by stoning an Arab car -- offences that carry a 24-year maximum sentence.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinians in January but kept soldiers in the other 20 percent to safeguard 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
Hebron is holy to Moslem and Jew as the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham.
